slides.label: Definition Card

params.definition: The tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of motion.
params.example: A passenger continues moving forward when a bus stops suddenly.

slides.narration: Inertia is an object's tendency to resist a change in motion. Greater mass means greater inertia.

slides.label: Comparison Table
slides.narration: Scalars have magnitude only, while vectors carry both magnitude and direction.

slides.label: Numerical Example
slides.narration: Write the equation, substitute the known values, and calculate the answer with its unit.

slides.label: Projectile Motion
slides.narration: Horizontal velocity remains constant while gravity continuously changes the vertical velocity component.

slides.label: Circular Motion
slides.narration: Velocity is always tangent to the circle, while centripetal force points toward its centre.

slides.label: Spring Mass
slides.narration: The restoring force reverses at each extreme and is proportional to displacement from equilibrium.

slides.label: Inclined Plane
slides.narration: Weight resolves into components parallel and perpendicular to the slope, while friction opposes motion.

slides.label: Thermal Heating
slides.narration: Temperature rises until boiling, then remains constant while energy separates the particles.

slides.label: EM Spectrum
slides.narration: The visible region is a narrow part of the electromagnetic spectrum between infrared and ultraviolet.

slides.label: Standing Wave
slides.narration: The third harmonic contains three loops, four nodes, and three antinodes.

slides.label: Electron Flow
slides.narration: Electrons drift through the conductor and transfer energy during collisions in the resistance zone.

slides.label: Motor Effect
slides.narration: Fleming's left-hand rule predicts the force direction from the magnetic field and current directions.

slides.label: EM Induction
slides.narration: Moving the magnet changes magnetic flux through the coil and induces a changing electromotive force.

slides.label: Transformer
slides.narration: Four times fewer turns on the secondary coil steps two hundred forty volts down to sixty volts.

slides.label: Gas Particles
slides.narration: Compressing the gas increases collision frequency, so the pressure on the container walls rises.

slides.label: Nuclear Reaction
slides.narration: A uranium nucleus absorbs a neutron, becomes unstable, and splits into smaller nuclei while releasing energy.

slides.label: Ray Diagram
slides.narration: Principal rays converge to form a real inverted image on the far side of the lens.

slides.label: Orbital Motion
slides.narration: Gravity always points toward Earth while orbital velocity stays tangent to the elliptical path.

slides.label: Star Life Cycle
slides.narration: A massive star evolves from a nebula to a supergiant before exploding as a supernova and potentially forming a black hole.

slides.label: Radiation Penetration
slides.narration: Paper stops alpha, aluminium stops beta, and thick concrete is needed to stop highly penetrating gamma radiation.
